I farm sorghum the way my father taught me, using seed I kept from last harvest and cow dung from my animals. I do not buy chemical fertilizer because it costs too much and the cooperative never brings it on time here in Afar, and you cannot trust the rain. My family will work the land ourselves — about fifty days spread across planting, weeding, and harvest — because hiring labor is something only people with cash can do.
